title: The Radiolysis of Water Ice Interfaces and of Aromatic Compounds Studied by Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy
content: While the radiolysis of liquid water by high-energy electrons has been extensively studied by conventional radiation chemistry methods, the radiolysis of water at interfaces and inside an electron microscope and the radiolysis of water ice are still poorly understood. Electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) can be performed inside the scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM), and thus, can allow for in situ analysis of radiation damage effects. In frozen hydrated aqueous specimens, cryo-EELS has already been used to study radiation damage.[1-3] Using new monochromated sources, with higher energy resolutions on the order of < 100 meV[4] and increased peak(signal)-to-background (S/B) ratio, new insights on the radiation damage of materials have been recently made possible.
